sources.entry: ossu/computer-science: free self-taught education in Computer Science!

summary.one_liner: A self-directed, community-supported computer science curriculum that strings together free online courses and books into a roughly bachelor's-level CS education.
summary.what_it_does: The README lays out an ordered curriculum in three tiers: Intro CS, Core CS (programming, math, CS tools, systems, theory, security, applications, ethics), and Advanced CS electives grouped by subject. Each section is a table of courses with duration, weekly effort, prerequisites, and links to discussion chats. Courses are chosen to be open for enrollment, run regularly or self-paced, and match the CS 2013 guidelines, with books substituted where no course fits. It ends with a final project section that suggests project-oriented courses and specializations. It also points to a Discord community, a GitHub issues process for curriculum changes, and a suggested method of tracking progress by forking the repo and ticking completed items. A spreadsheet is offered for estimating completion dates.
use_cases: Teach myself computer science without a degree
Find free online courses in a structured order
Plan a self-study path over about two years
Find free CS course sequence with prerequisites listed
Track progress through a CS curriculum
Choose electives in a chosen CS specialty
how_to_run: Fork the GitHub repository into your own account
Read the curriculum sections in order, starting with Prerequisites and Intro CS
Follow the course links in each table and check prerequisites before starting
Mark completed courses with a checkmark in your fork
Optionally copy the timeline spreadsheet linked in the README to estimate your end date
stack: Online course platforms (linked courses from Harvard, Princeton, MIT and others, including Coursera and edX as mentioned)
notable: Organized as a full CS degree equivalent using free online courses and books
Each course table lists duration, weekly effort, prerequisites and a discussion chat
Advanced CS electives grouped by subject so learners pick one focus area
Explicit selection criteria: open enrollment, regular runs, teaching quality, CS 2013 alignment
Community of learners on Discord and GitHub issues for curriculum changes
caveats: Requires strong self-discipline and time, about 20 hours per week for a two-year pace
Some courses charge for graded assignments, tests or projects, though most material is free
The README warns that the timeline spreadsheet and some third-party materials may be outdated; the OSSU website and repo are the authoritative sources
keywords: learn computer science on my own
free alternative to a cs degree
